Mitigation Proposal: Closed-Loop Crusher Load Control via Specific Power Optimization

Mechanism:
Implement a real-time feedback control strategy that regulates the crusher’s closing speed based on the ratio of specific power to throughput, using only existing motor power and belt scale data. The goal is to minimize the specific energy consumption (kWh/ton) while ensuring the discharge product remains within the desired size range by preventing the crusher from overloading.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
All signals and actuators must conform to the constraint: use only existing sensors (crusher motor power meter, feed-rate scale, discharge-belt scale). No new instrumentation may be added.

1. Inputs and Derived Metrics:
   • P_motor (kW): Instantaneous power draw, measured directly by the crusher motor power meter.
   • M_discharge (t/h): Mass flow rate of crusher product, measured directly by the discharge-belt scale.
   • M_feed (t/h): Input mass flow rate, measured directly by the feed-rate scale.
   • SP (kW·h/ton): Specific Power, derived by formula SP = P_motor / M_discharge.

2. Control Logic:
   • Reference: SP_max is derived from historical data of the last liner change (optimal performance point). This is a parameter derived from existing records, not a new sensor input.
   • Actuator: The manipulated variable is the crusher’s closing speed, controlled via the existing variable speed drive or hydraulic system.
   • Logic Rule:
     If SP > SP_max, execute command to decrease closing speed.
     If SP < SP_min (derived from optimal zone lower bound), execute command to increase closing speed.

3. Material Balance Validation:
   • Monitor M_feed and M_discharge. Ensure consistency (M_feed ≈ M_discharge + stock changes) to validate that the SP metric is stable and not skewed by transient scale errors. This uses only the existing feed-rate and discharge-belt scales.

DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT STATEMENT:
• Driving Variable: Specific Power (SP), which is inversely related to crushing efficiency when load is excessive.
• Direction of Effect: An increase in SP indicates the crusher is overloaded or processing coarse material inefficiently. To counteract this and restore optimal operation, the control loop must actuate the closing speed in the direction of DECREASE. Lowering the closing speed reduces the crushing intensity, allowing material to discharge more easily, which lowers the power draw per ton of product (reducing SP) and improves particle size distribution, thereby reducing the coarse fraction and recycle load.

Why This Works:
The failure mode of coarsened product and high power per ton indicates the crusher is running at excessive intensity for the given feed. By closing the loop on Specific Power using only permitted existing sensors, the system automatically backs off the crushing intensity when inefficiency rises, restoring optimal operation without adding new instrumentation.
